cards.text: David, Israel's king, calls in all his leaders, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds. Then he speaks to the whole assembly of Israel, and he's got a BIG plan. But first he checks with them: only if it seems good to them, and only if it's of the LORD their God.

cards.question: Before his plan starts, David wants to send word far and wide. Who does he want to come join them?

answers.text: All their brothers plus the priests and Levites
The kings of the nearby nations

cards.question: David's big plan: all of Israel together will bring back the ___ of God.
David looks back to the days of Saul, the king before him. Why does he say they should bring the ark back?

answers.text: They did not inquire of Him in Saul's days
The Philistines are planning to capture it
The priests have begged him to bring it

cards.question: When David shares his plan, half the assembly turns it down.

cards.text: Nope. It seems right to all the people, so the whole assembly agrees, and David gathers all Israel, from the River Shihor in Egypt all the way to Lebo-hamath.
And I thought the junk drawer was crowded. They all go up to Baalah of Judah, also called Kiriath-jearim, to bring up the ark of God the LORD, who is enthroned between the cherubim.

cards.question: The ark of God has been kept in the house of Abinadab, a man in Kiriath-jearim (1 Samuel 7:1). Now they bring it out of his house. What do they carry it on?

cards.text: A NEW cart, with two men, Uzzah and Ahio, guiding it. I bet that thing still has the price sticker on the wheel.

cards.question: As the cart rolls along with the ark, it's a quiet and solemn march for David and the Israelites.

cards.text: Quiet? NO. Songs, harps, lyres, tambourines, cymbals AND trumpets, all celebrating before God with all their might! That's me when a batch comes out perfect, hopping on my gold base till the whole bakery shakes.
Then the whole parade reaches the threshing floor of Chidon. And the oxen stumble.

cards.question: The oxen pulling the cart stumble at the threshing floor of Chidon. What does Uzzah do?

answers.text: He takes hold of the ark
He jumps down to calm the oxen
He shouts for everyone to stop

cards.text: Then the anger of the LORD burns against Uzzah, and He strikes him down. Uzzah dies right there before God.

cards.question: The text gives the reason: the LORD struck Uzzah down because he had put his ___ on the ark.
When the LORD bursts forth against Uzzah, David becomes angry.

cards.text: David names that place Perez-uzzah, and it's still called that to this day. And that same day, David fears God.

cards.question: That day at Perez-uzzah, David fears God. What does David ask?

answers.text: How can I ever bring the ark of God to me
Who will guide the cart from here on
Where should we go to bury Uzzah

cards.question: David goes ahead and takes the ark with him to the City of David.

cards.text: Instead, David takes it aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite. Picture opening your front door, and the KING is standing there asking if you can hold onto something for a while.

cards.question: The ark of God stays with the family of Obed-edom in his house for three ___.
While the ark of God stays at his house, what happens to Obed-edom's household?

answers.text: The LORD blesses it and all he owns
His family grows afraid and leaves
Sickness spreads all through his house

cards.text: So the ark sits at Obed-edom's house, not in the City of David. Hang onto your apron, friend, because we're only one batch into this story.

findings.problem: This fill-in-the-blank asks what David's plan is about, the ark, but no story card has set it up. Card 1 says only that David has a 'BIG plan,' and card 2 is a choice card. The baker reaches four choice cards in a row and has to guess between ark, altar and tent with nothing told to reason from.

rule.text: The setup for a choice is on a story card. Not every choice card needs its own story card right before it: a choice card can follow another choice card when the setup is already told.

findings.problem: Uzzah, the central figure of the passage, and Ahio are introduced only as 'two men.' That doesn't say who they are. They could be introduced as sons of Abinadab, with the reference (2 Samuel 6:3).

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: This story card runs four sentences: 'Quiet?' 'NO.' the list of instruments, and the gold-base joke. A non-opening story card is limited to 1 to 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: 'The text gives the reason:' frames the card as a reading-comprehension test, not as Papa Dorin pausing mid-story.

rule.text: Ask from inside the passage, the way a storyteller pauses to let the listener lean in. The question comes out of the moment Papa Dorin just set up.

findings.problem: The joke mixes the modern front-door picture with the Bible setting, since the KING is the one at the door. It also reads as if David came to Obed-edom and asked him to keep the ark. The text says only that David took it aside to his house (13:13).

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: The first sentence, 'So the ark sits at Obed-edom's house, not in the City of David,' repeats what cards 8 and 9 already told, and the card cites 13:13 again for it. The last verse, 13:14, is asked on choice cards, so this card can be just the story-isn't-over line.
